requirements.requirement: Enough eligible RRMM patients: adults, 1-4 prior lines including lenalidomide and a proteasome inhibitor, progression per 2016 IMWG; about 410 randomized 1:1 worldwide
requirements.source: protocol.md: Inclusion 1, 3; Phase 3, randomized 1:1, planned enrollment 410

requirements.requirement: Exclude patients who have had pomalidomide or elotuzumab
Exclude patients who have had BCMA-directed immunotherapy (BCMA ADCs allowed)

Document the full prior treatment history: number of lines, lenalidomide-refractory status for 1-line patients, CD38 exposure (a stratification subgroup), last anticancer therapy date for the 28-day / 5-half-life washout, and timing of autologous or allogeneic transplant
requirements.source: protocol.md: Inclusion 3; Exclusion 4, 5; Outcomes (CD38 antibody exposed participants)

requirements.requirement: Investigator assessment of ECOG 0-1 (ECOG 2 from myeloma pain after Medical Monitor discussion), life expectancy of at least 6 months, active infection, and a neurologic history and exam to exclude PML, neurocognitive disorder or Parkinsonism

Lab testing for screening and response: SPEP, UPEP, immunofixation, serum free light chains for measurable disease and IMWG response; hematology, chemistry, renal function and corrected calcium within 7 days of randomization; HIV, HBV and HCV serology and viral load
requirements.source: protocol.md: Inclusion 4, 5; Exclusion 9; Outcomes (IMWG response by investigator and IRC)

requirements.requirement: Cardiac function testing: LVEF by echocardiogram or MUGA to exclude EF below 40%, plus ECG
requirements.source: protocol.md: Inclusion 5 (adequate cardiac function); Exclusion 10 (ejection fraction <40%)

requirements.requirement: Diagnostic workup to exclude plasma cell leukemia, amyloidosis, Waldenstrom and POEMS (bone marrow biopsy, pathology, peripheral smear); CNS imaging (MRI) to exclude brain or meningeal myeloma when suspected; skeletal/extramedullary imaging (CT, PET-CT or MRI) for IMWG response
Bone marrow aspirate and biopsy at screening and to confirm CR and MRD, with fresh aspirate shipped to a central MRD lab and M-protein samples sent for IRC review
requirements.source: protocol.md: Outcomes (MRD negative status in the bone marrow; OR/PFS by Independent Review Committee)

requirements.requirement: Processing (centrifuge) and frozen storage (-70 C or colder) of serum PK, ADA and neutralizing-antibody samples, with batch shipping
requirements.source: protocol.md: Outcomes (linvoseltamab serum concentration; ADA incidence/titer; NAbs)

requirements.requirement: Patient-reported outcomes collected at visits: BPI-SF Item 3 worst pain, EORTC QLQ-C30, QLQ-MY20, PGIS, PGIC, EQ-5D-5L
requirements.source: protocol.md: Outcomes (BPI-SF, EORTC QLQ-C30, QLQ-MY20, PGIS, PGIC, EQ-5D-5L)

requirements.requirement: 24-hour inpatient monitoring after linvoseltamab step-up dose 1 (5 mg, Day 1) and step-up dose 2 (25 mg, Day 8), with step-up and re-hospitalization repeated after dose delays; patients need a caregiver or transport because they may not drive for 48 hours after each step-up dose

CRS and neurologic toxicity/ICANS (boxed warning): trained staff for ASTCT CRS grading and ICE scoring, tocilizumab and steroids available right away, ICU and neurology backup, 24/7 investigator coverage

LYNOZYFIC REMS for commercial product (certified prescribers and healthcare settings; patient wallet card and counseling); pretreatment with acetaminophen, diphenhydramine and dexamethasone 40 mg before step-up doses and the first full dose
Infection, neutropenia and hypogammaglobulinemia management: CBC and IgG monitoring, PJP and herpesvirus prophylaxis, IVIG

Long-term IV visit load: linvoseltamab weekly Weeks 4-13, every 2 weeks from Week 14, every 4 weeks for VGPR or better at Week 24+ (30-60 minute infusions); elotuzumab IV weekly in cycles 1-2 then every 4 weeks, with premedication and infusion-reaction observation
EPd comparator: pomalidomide under its REMS (certified prescriber and pharmacy, pregnancy testing and contraception counseling, 28-day supply limit); weight-based elotuzumab preparation

Staff capacity: research coordinators and data staff for frequent visits, PROs and long-term survival follow-up; investigational pharmacy to store, prepare and account for linvoseltamab and EPd; sub-investigators
requirements.source: protocol.md: Outcomes (OS; DoR; duration of MRD negativity: long-term follow-up); Phase 3, enrollment 410

requirements.requirement: No local competition for the same lenalidomide/PI-exposed, BCMA-naive RRMM patients
Fast start-up: contract, budget and IRB approval in time for the recruitment window

questionnaire.question: How many new patients with relapsed/refractory myeloma after 1-4 prior lines (including lenalidomide and a proteasome inhibitor) does your myeloma program see per year?
Of those patients, about what percentage have never received pomalidomide?
Of those patients, about what percentage have never received a BCMA-directed bispecific or CAR-T?
For patients referred from outside practices, how often are complete prior-therapy records (regimens, dates, best response, progression) available at the screening visit?
How many minutes does your investigational pharmacy usually need to prepare and release an IV investigational dose after the order?
Can your site ship fresh bone marrow aspirate to a central lab by overnight courier on the day of collection?
Does your research lab have a temperature-monitored freezer at -70 C or colder for study serum samples?
Can your staff give sponsor-provided electronic PRO tablets to patients at clinic visits?
How reliably can your site schedule a planned 24-hour inpatient admission for a step-up dose day?
Is tocilizumab stocked so it can be given within 2 hours of a CRS diagnosis, 24/7?
Are the nurses on the unit that would admit step-up patients trained in ICE scoring for ICANS?
Is your pharmacy certified to dispense pomalidomide under its REMS?
How many days' lead time does your infusion center need to book a recurring weekly infusion chair slot?
How many research coordinator FTEs could your myeloma team assign to this study?
How many trials for the same population (RRMM, 1-4 prior lines, BCMA-naive) do you expect to open at your site in the next 12 months that are not yet public?
How many weeks does your site typically take from receipt of the final protocol to an executed clinical trial agreement and budget for an industry Phase 3 trial?

# Riverside Cancer Research Office: what we share in feasibility responses

Share with sponsors:
- Aggregate patient numbers (counts, percentages), capabilities, our own timelines, rates and fees.

Never share:
- Anything about an individual patient: MRN, initials, age, visit dates, regimens or notes of a specific person.
- Pipeline trials under confidentiality agreement (CDA): we may say how many are planned, never the sponsor, drug or trial code.

- CRS grading per ASTCT consensus; ICE score assessed by trained nursing every 12 hours during step-up dosing.

- ICU transfer pathway for grade 3+ CRS or ICANS (ICU in same building).

## About
Riverside Cancer Center is the cancer program of Riverside Medical Center in Dayton, Ohio. Our hematology team treats lymphoma, leukemia and multiple myeloma, led by Dr. Elena Marsh (Myeloma Program Lead).

## Services
- Infusion center with 16 chairs
- Inpatient oncology unit (6 West) and an ICU in the same building
- On-site MRI, CT, echocardiography and bone marrow procedures
- Accredited by the Commission on Cancer. Laboratory CAP accredited.

## For sponsors: Clinical Trials Office
The Riverside Cancer Research Office handles feasibility, contracts, budgets and regulatory startup for industry trials. We accept local Riverside IRB or WCG central IRB review. To send a feasibility questionnaire, use the sponsor intake form on this page.

## For patients and families
Patients traveling for treatment can stay at the Riverside Inn, our partner hotel 10 minutes away, at a discounted rate.
